from.place: ## Proof, affine case: the sentence identifying the cohomology via the vanishing of the higher direct images at the finitely many boundary points

title: Boundary higher direct images of the multiplicative group vanish
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $\bar C$ be a proper smooth connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves], let $S$ be a finite set of closed points of $\bar C$, put $C=\bar C\setminus S$, and let $j:C\to\bar C$ be the open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every geometric point $\bar x$ of $\bar C$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], the stalks $(R^qj_*\mathbf G_m)_{\bar x}$ vanish for $q=1,2$, where higher direct images and the etale sheaf of units are as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and [def-sc-gm-torsor].

source.place: Discussion preceding Tag 03RM, computation of stalks of R^q j_* G_m using strict henselizations

proof.text: The open immersion $j$ is quasi-compact because $C$ is an open subscheme of the Noetherian curve $\bar C$, and quasi-separated because it is an open immersion. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-gm-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] to $f=j$: for every geometric point $\bar x$, $(R^qj_*\mathbf G_m)_{\bar x}$ is, by the last assertion of that statement, $H^q((C\times_{\bar C}\bar C_{(\bar x)})_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf G_m)$, where $\bar C_{(\bar x)}$ is the strict henselization at $\bar x$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), specialized to j and G_m

proof.text: If $\bar x$ lies over a point of $C$, some open neighbourhood $V$ of that point in $\bar C$ lies in $C$. Over $V$, $j$ is the identity, whose direct-image functor is exact; restriction to $V$ therefore makes $R^qj_*\mathbf G_m$ zero for every $q>0$. Its stalk at $\bar x$ is zero.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03RJ (lemma-higher-direct-jstar-Gm), geometric-stalk argument adapted to an interior point

proof.text: If $\bar x$ lies over $P\in S$, [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] makes $A=\mathcal O_{\bar C,P}$ a Noetherian DVR with fraction field $k(\bar C)$. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr] applied to $Y=\bar C$, $A^{\mathrm{sh}}=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\bar C,\bar x}$ is again a DVR and $A\to A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is a flat local, hence injective, homomorphism. The base change $C\times_{\bar C}\operatorname{Spec}(A^{\mathrm{sh}})$ is the open subscheme of points not mapping to $P$; it removes exactly the closed point: the closed point maps to $P$ (locality), while the generic point maps to the generic point of $\bar C$ (the injection $A\to A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ of domains pulls back the zero ideal to the zero ideal), which lies in $C$. Thus it is $\operatorname{Spec}K$ for $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A^{\mathrm{sh}})\supset k(\bar C)$. Each element of $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ comes from an etale neighbourhood of $P$, whose fraction field is finite algebraic over $k(\bar C)$; hence $K/k(\bar C)$ is algebraic. For $q=1$, [cor-sc-hilbert-90-field] gives $H^1((\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf G_m)=0$. For $q=2$, apply [lem-sc-brauer-algebraic-function-field-zero] with $L=E=K$ (the degree-one separable extension) to obtain $H^2((\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf G_m)=0$. The stalks in Step 1 therefore vanish.
